speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you are presenting with a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. Can you describe how this lesion started and if you have noticed any changes in its appearance or size over time?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that detailed history. Given your history of Crohn's disease and diabetes, I need to rule out specific inflammatory or infectious causes. Does the ulcer have a raised, violaceous border, and have you experienced any recent gastrointestinal symptoms like diarrhea or abdominal pain?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Painful ulcerative lesion on the right leg. I also have Lesion has a central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, History of ant bite at the site of the lesion, Pitting pedal edema of the lower extremities, Dilated tortuous veins in both lower legs.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The history of an ant bite at the site, combined with the central necrotic base and purplish irregular borders, strongly suggests a specific diagnosis, though your vascular findings are notable. Given the trauma history and lesion characteristics, I am confident in my assessment.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Pyoderma Gangrenosum
